### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §2.2 Proposition 2.8 (printed p. 35; PDF p. 44) — item `awodey:2.2:prop8`. Awodey states that initial objects (dually, terminal objects) are unique up to a *unique* isomorphism; this is the same obligation as MacLane's uniqueness of terminal/initial/zero objects.

In-tree status: the general `univ_property_unique_up_to_unique_iso` (`Structure/UniversalProperty.v:175`) proves uniqueness up to unique iso for any representing object of a universal property, but `Terminal`/`Initial` (`Structure/Terminal.v`, `Structure/Initial.v`) are never instantiated into that framework, so no standalone “any two terminal (resp. initial) objects are uniquely isomorphic” lemma exists (a derivation is possible via `Terminal_Limit` → `LimitIsUniversalProperty`). Awodey adds no obligation beyond this issue. Minor: the `Theory/Isomorphism.v:83` header already calls the terminal object “the simplest instance” of this uniqueness, but the instantiation is not carried out.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §2.4 (printed p. 42; PDF p. 51), the prose definition of a projective object — item `awodey:2.4:def-projective`. Awodey defines `P` projective iff for every epi `e : E ↠ X` and every `f : P → X` there is a (not necessarily unique) lift `f̄ : P → E` with `e ∘ f̄ = f`. This is exactly the projective-object notion (left lifting against epimorphisms) of this issue.

In-tree status: no `Projective` class exists (`grep -rniE '(Class|Definition|Record).*[Pp]rojective'` → 0 hits; “projective” occurs only in essay prose such as “enough projectives”). Awodey’s examples and axiom-of-choice content (every set/`Pos` object projective; retract closure) are filed as a dependent Awodey issue (`awodey:2.4:example15`, `awodey:2:ex3`) that depends on this one. No obligation beyond this issue for the definition itself.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §2.6 (printed p. 45; PDF p. 54), the worked example of the componentwise product of monoids/groups — item `awodey:2.6:construction-product-monoid-group`. Awodey exhibits `G × H` (cartesian product of underlying sets, componentwise operation/unit/inverse, projections homomorphisms) as the categorical product in **Mon**/**Grp**; same obligation as finite products in the category of monoids (the group case is the evident analogue).

In-tree status: the componentwise product is a genuine categorical product only for commutative monoids (`Instance/CMon/Biproduct.v:442` `CMon_Biproduct`) and the equation-free signature category (`Instance/Comp.v:169` `Algs_Cartesian`). For the equational variety **Mon**/**Grp** (`Instance/Comp.v:434` `Product`, `:426` `Project`) only the product *object* and homomorphism projections are built, not the pairing/UMP.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §2.6 (printed p. 46; PDF p. 55), the worked example that the product in a poset is the greatest lower bound — item `awodey:2.6:construction-product-poset`. Awodey shows that for elements `p, q` of a poset-as-category the product `p × q` is their meet (glb); same obligation as products in a preorder are greatest lower bounds.

In-tree status: the general theorem is absent — `Instance/Poset.v` and `Instance/Proset.v` carry no `Cartesian` instance (`grep` confirms Cartesian-instance files exclude them). The product = meet identity is realized only for concrete thin categories: `Instance/Props.v:69` `Props_Cartesian` (conjunction = meet) and `Instance/Two/Monoidal.v:37` `two_meet`.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §2.6 (printed pp. 46–47; PDF pp. 55–56), the worked example of the product of topological spaces — item `awodey:2.6:construction-product-top`. Awodey shows the product space `X × Y` (product topology, generated by basic opens `U × V`) with its projections is the product in **Top**; this binary product is subsumed by **Top**’s completeness (this issue).

In-tree status: no category **Top** exists — `grep -rli 'topological space|homeomorph|open subset'` → 0 hits across the tree, there is no `Instance/Top.v`, and no continuity/open-set structure anywhere — so both **Top** and its products are absent.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §2.7 (printed p. 51; PDF p. 60), the construction of finite (ternary / n-ary) products from binary products — item `awodey:2.7:construction-finite-products`. Awodey builds `A × B × C := (A × B) × C` and argues a category with binary products has all finite products (≥ 2 factors), the binary product being associative up to iso; the reduction “terminal + binary ⇒ all finite products” is exactly this issue’s obligation.

In-tree status: associativity up to iso is already present (`Structure/Cartesian.v:485` `prod_assoc`; also Awodey Exercise 6, present), and the n-ary UMP exists as an independent discrete-limit primitive (`Structure/Limit/Product.v:51` `IsIndexedProduct`), but no theorem derives the n-ary product by *iterating* the binary one and proving its n-ary UMP that way (`grep` for a Cartesian → finite-products bridge is empty).

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §2.9 Exercise 1 (printed p. 55; PDF p. 64) — item `awodey:2:ex1`. Awodey asks to show a function between sets is surjective iff it is an epimorphism in `Set`; identical obligation to “epis in `Sets` are exactly the surjections”.

In-tree status: `Instance/Sets.v:429` `surjectivity_is_epic` states the biconditional but ends in `Abort` (the forward surjective→epic branch is a complete script *inside* the aborted proof; the reverse epic→surjective branch is abandoned owing to the documented subobject-classifier size obstruction, `Instance/Sets/Classifier.v`), so nothing enters the environment. Same missing direction (epic → surjective) as this issue.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §2.9 Exercise 2 (printed p. 55; PDF p. 64), parts (a)–(d) — item `awodey:2:ex2`. For a commutative triangle `h = g ∘ f`: (a) `f, g` both isos/monos/epis ⇒ `h` is; (b) `h` monic ⇒ `f` monic; (c) `h` epic ⇒ `g` epic; (d) an example with `h` monic but `g` not monic. Parts (b)/(c) are exactly the single-factor monic/epi cancellation of this issue, and (d) is a “non-invertible” witness in its spirit.

In-tree status: part (a) is fully present (`Theory/Morphisms.v:213` `monic_compose`, `:201` `epi_compose`, `Theory/Isomorphism.v:166` `iso_compose`); the single-factor cancellation lemmas (`g ∘ f` monic ⇒ `f` monic; `g ∘ f` epic ⇒ `g` epic) and the counterexample (d) are absent (the `≈`-transport lemmas in `Structure/Abelian.v:387/399` are a different fact).

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §2.9 Exercise 4 (printed p. 55; PDF p. 64) — item `awodey:2:ex4`. For a set `A`, Awodey defines the category `A`-**Mon** of monoids `M` with a function `A → U(M)` (arrows: monoid homomorphisms commuting with the structure maps) and asks to show that an initial object of `A`-**Mon** is the same thing as a free monoid `M(A)` on `A`, by comparing universal properties.

The mathematical content is the free-monoid universal property of this issue: `A`-**Mon** is the comma category `(A ↓ U)` for the underlying-set functor `U : Mon → Set`, and “initial object of the comma = universal arrow = free monoid” is the standard reformulation (MacLane III.1 universal arrows, in-tree machinery). In-tree status: no category **Mon** and no free-monoid construction/UMP exist (`Instance/CMon.v` is commutative monoids; `Theory/Coq/List.v` calls `list A` the underlying set of the free monoid only in prose, with no UMP). Awodey adds the `A`-**Mon** comma presentation but no obligation beyond the free-monoid universal property.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §2.9 Exercise 7 (printed p. 56; PDF p. 65), parts (a)–(b) — item `awodey:2:ex7`. Part (a) asks to define the `I`-indexed product `∏_{i∈I} X_i` by a UMP generalizing the binary case; part (b) asks to show the function set `X^I` satisfies this UMP for the constant family `X_i = X`, so `X^I ≅ ∏_{i∈I} X` in `Set`.

In-tree status: part (a) is already present at full (indeed arbitrary-Type-indexed) strength — `Structure/Limit/Product.v:51` `IsIndexedProduct`. Part (b) — `Set` having the `I`-indexed product of a family, hence `X^I` for the constant family — is the small-completeness-of-`Sets` obligation of this issue (`Instance/Sets/Cartesian.v` provides only *binary* products; there is no small/indexed product in `Sets` and no `X^I ≅ ∏X` construction). Awodey’s `X^I` is the constant-family special case.
